To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the susceptibility to virus entry is dependent on the organization of the vimentin network and the activities of the protein kinase C isoforms PKCα and ε.
the efficiency of infection/transduction by viruses depends upon cell line-specific features, which can be modified by the choice of medium.
cell susceptibility to virus infection and gene transfer is modulated by the organization of cytoskeleton and protein phosphorylation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms involved in the regulation of virus infection and transduction.

the cell line-dependent differences in the efficiency of infection/transduction by EV1 or BV, which is associated with the expression levels of PKCα, vimentin organization and phosphorylation, and the expression levels of the adaptor molecule syntenin.
a better understanding of the mechanisms involved in virus infection or gene transfer and the development of strategies to improve viral transduction efficiency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cell lines that are nonpermissive for viral infection and transduction are characterized by the presence of a dense vimentin network and the absence of pPKCα, whereas the presence of pPKCε and a loose vimentin network are associated with permissive cells.
the nonpermissive nature in the nonpermissive cells was due to the lack of PKCα and pPKCα activation and a disorganized vimentin network.
the nonpermissive nature is a result of a combination of events that occur in the nonpermissive cells and are not present in the permissive cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PKCα, vimentin and PKCε are key players in virus entry and transduction, respectively.
PKCα and vimentin are the key factors affecting efficient transduction and infection by EV1 and baculovirus, respectively.

PKCα and/or PKCε activity is necessary and sufficient for efficient infection/transduction, and the vimentin network is the downstream target of these kinases that is required for efficient virus internalization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vimentin cytoskeleton and PKCα and ε are critical factors that influence viral infection and gene delivery.
the efficiency of virus infection/transduction can be modified by altering the vimentin network and PKC activity in the cell.

the cell-line-specific susceptibility to virus transduction and infection is not solely determined by the number and activity of viral receptors but also depends on the intracellular signaling pathways that are activated upon virus attachment to the cell surface.
